records.title: Public money to political money (stage 1: inventory and search plan)
The check: an official on the Nov 3, 2026 ballot took an official action that directed or approved public money to an
organization, and that organization (or an organization an official record shows it paid) then gave money to a
political committee or candidate. Stage 1 lists the recipients and says how to search for their political giving.
Motivating case: Ashley Moody (Attorney General 2019-2025, on the ballot for U.S. Senate). The Sept. 27, 2024 Centene
settlement, to which the State was a party "by and through its Attorney General", directed $10M of the State's
recovery to The Hope Florida Foundation, Inc. (manual-actions.json). Press reports say the foundation then sent $5M
each to Secure Florida's Future and Save Our Society From Drugs, which gave to Keep Florida Clean, the committee
against 2024 Amendment 3. Each of those links still needs its own official record (below).
Never cite the Leon County grand jury presentment on Hope Florida.** The 1st DCA expunged it on Oct 7, 2026.
(a) An official action** by the official that directed or approved public money to recipient R: a yes vote on an
award, contract, grant, funding item or change order naming R; a budget or earmark request the official filed for R;
a grant the official's own office made to R; a settlement or agreement the official's office signed that directs
public money (money the State recovered or holds) to R. The action file must give the official's vote or act from
the body's own record. `unknown` votes (minutes give none) never make a flag. A budget request counts only for the
money that made the final budget (`funded`).
(b) An official contribution record** showing R, or a recipient R2 that an official record shows R paid (e.g.
R's IRS Form 990 Schedule I grants list, R2's 990 revenue lines, a DOE or FEC report listing R as the source of a
transfer), gave money to a political committee or candidate **within 24 months after R received the money**. The
receipt date is the payment date when a record gives it, otherwise the action date (say which).
Show the chain link by link, each with its record: action (official, date, amount, record URL), then each payment
(who, to whom, date, amount, record URL). Nothing in the chain may come from press reports alone; press can point to
Never say or suggest the official intended, arranged or knew of the later giving. Say what the records show,
Never connect two records on a shared name alone. A contribution row is R's only when the name matches **and** the
contributor address on the row matches an address an official record gives for R (the action record, R's Sunbiz
principal or mailing address, R's IRS filing address), or the row carries an ID that matches (FEC committee ID,
DOE account number). A name-only hit is kept as `unconfirmed` and never shown.
Never understate. When a search was partial (a record not reachable, a row limit hit, a year not online), totals
The money must be public: tax dollars, State or local funds, federal pass-through grants, or money the government
recovered and directed (a settlement's settlement amount). A private party's own payment that no government

Built from the published action lists, so it follows the same standard as the site (scripts/data/tenure/STANDARD.md,
current seats: `public/data/decisions/<body>.json`, each on-ballot member's own yes votes and budget or earmark
requests (state requests carry the final-budget status from the General Appropriations Act and veto list);
earlier seats: `public/data/prior/<pid>.json` (scripts/prior-offices.mjs): council, commission, school board and
Cabinet votes, the Attorney General's office grants (Division of Victim Services annual reports, FY 2019-20 to
2023-24, non-government grantees), FDACS's own easement purchases, and earlier legislative budget requests. If
that folder is empty because a rebuild is running, the script reads the committed copy;
addresses, only where a record gives one: the action record (tenure action files) and the House CPF tables
Left out and counted in `counts`: government bodies (cities, counties, school boards, agencies, public universities
and colleges, districts, authorities), names that look like a person (listed in `peopleLeftOut` so a business
misread as a person can be put back), placeholders such as "contractor (not named in minutes)" (`placeholdersLeftOut`),
and the Attorney General's own settlements where a company pays the State (no public money to the company).
`actions[].money` is `paid` when the kind is a payment to the party, `unclear` when it can run either way
(agreement, settlement, lease, land: read the record). `qualifying` counts actions with a yes, request or act and
`money: paid`. Grouping is by name with suffixes stripped; two rows of one key are the same name, not proven the same
entity. Amounts over $5 billion on a local item are flagged `amountSuspect` (a parsing error upstream: e.g. "$6300000
million" in scripts/data/tenure/prior-county/actions.json, county items 110851 and 072312) and left out of ranking.

The congress slice screened 108th-116th laws by rule (build/rules.py there). For this window every law was read instead,
as the congress slice did for the 117th-118th: all 171 laws whose final CRS summary has a business keyword were read
sentence by sentence, and the other 367 (ceremonial or no keyword) were scanned by title and summary. Result: the
congress slice's 20 qualifying laws plus 39 more (build/adds.py lists each with its quoted sentence), 59 in all. The
same test applies: the CRS summary itself must say a kind of business benefits (payments, tax breaks, regulatory relief,
liability shields, license or deadline extensions, conveyances, multiyear procurement); a business only regulated or
burdened does not count. Borderline laws left out: VA Choice (113-146, 114-41: care purchased from providers),
114-60 (PACE Act), 114-61 (American Samoa minimum wage), 114-74 (Bipartisan Budget Act 2015: crop-insurer return cap and
outpatient site-neutral cut are burdens), 114-159 (miscellaneous tariff process), 114-182 (TSCA), 114-201 (HOTMA).
Vote picks: build/rolls.py + pick2.py + pick3.py (copied from the congress slice) on the BILLSTATUS actions, with three
114-255 (21st Century Cures): the final House vote is roll 592 (2016-11-30, 392-26). pick2 missed it because the action
text is truncated, so the congress slice's universe shows this law as a voice vote for Diaz-Balart too. **Coordinator:
the same fix applies to scripts/data/tenure/congress/laws/universe-108-116.json (Diaz-Balart voted on roll 592).**
114-187 (PROMESA): S. 2328 was deemed passed under H.Res. 770 right after the House passed the same text as H.R. 5278
114-190 (FAA extension, fractional-aircraft ticket-tax exemption): the House agreed to the final text under H.Res. 818
without a recorded vote. pick2 had chosen roll 82 of Feb 2015, which was on the bill's original unrelated text.
Coordinator: the 39 added laws are 113th-114th laws that Diaz-Balart also voted on.** His universe-108-116.json does not
include them (rule screen). To keep one test for every member, either add these 39 (with his votes from the clerk XML)
or treat this folder's list as the 2014-2016 universe for all three.
Rolls above 999: none in 2013-2016. `rollYear` is set on each card vote so voteUrl() can build clerk.house.gov/Votes/YYYYNNN.
Committees from the cm/ccl masters (see offices.json). Same method as congress/build/fec_build.py: candidate committees'
PAC receipts are taken from the giver's 24K report (bulk itoth has no 11C lines), leadership PAC/JFC receipts from their
own 18K. Window: one cycle before the term to the term's last day (Jolly 2011-01-01 to 2017-01-03; Graham 2013-01-01
to 2017-01-03). Jolly's committee also carried his 2016 U.S. Senate run (July 2015 to June 2016) before he returned to the House
race; those receipts are inside his House term and are kept. JFC-multi rows are shared committees (not all for him).

and VOTE lines ("VOTE: 8-0. Commissioner Ryan was not present."). Members not named voted yes; abstained is stored as
`recused` (the city files use yes/no/absent/recused/unknown). Every tally was checked against the parsed roll (all 321
match after seating 8 members from Sep 8, 2022, when Commissioner Alston had left). Build: broward-src/bw_parse.py ->

records.title: Prior county offices: Barreiro (D5) and Gimenez (D7, Mayor)
Slice folder: scripts/data/tenure/prior-county/. Built 2026-10-25 from the Clerk of the Board's online minutes, the
Legistar matter pages, the Clerk's historical lobbyist registrations and Miami-Dade VoterFocus campaign reports. Nothing
here is merged into public/data; the coordinator decides how it counts.
actions.json: 7,752 final BCC actions 1998-06-16..2020-11-16 whose title names a private party (same envelope as
scripts/data/county/actions.json: window, sources, meetings, actions, gaps). Each action has the full roll keyed by the
Clerk's surname for every member seated that day (members not on the Board that day have no key), plus seated.Barreiro / seated.Gimenez,
lobbied (Clerk registrations), matter (requester, sponsors, memo From line, RECOMMENDATION text, veto lines),
veto (Clerk file type "Mayoral Veto", override roll calls) and, in Gimenez's mayoral window, a mayor block of raw facts.
unnamed.json: 25,940 final actions in the window left out (no named private party, or excluded by rule), with the reason.
vetoes.json: 28 veto override / veto sustained votes in the minutes, with rolls.
body.json: every member seated in the window (key, name, first and last meeting seen).
donors/: VoterFocus exports (same format as county/donors/*-campaign-*.csv), one file per campaign.
gifts-preview.json: preliminary name matches (party or registered lobbyist = contributor), for the coordinator to check.

Term: elected 1998-06-02 special election; first meeting 1998-06-16; last meeting 2018-03-21; seat vacant 2018-04-04
(careers.jsonl end 2018-03-31). Nov 2016..Mar 2018 done first, then back to 1998 (all in one pass).
Covered: 1998-06-16..2018-03-20 (BCC meetings; site-specific zoning hearings only from 2017-07-20).
Actions while seated: 6,763. His recorded vote: yes 5,048, no 82, absent/excused/recused 1,628,
vote not given 5. Actions with a registered lobbyist for a party: 928.
Preliminary matches on actions he voted on: 107 distinct contributions ($44,731.14) tied to 256 actions (gifts-preview.json).
Gaps: no campaign reports online for the 1998 special and 2000 races; no political committee tied to him by an official
record found (DOE check in needs-browser.md); zoning hearings 1998-06..2017-07 not online; lobbyist registrations before
mid-2003 only where the Clerk's per-principal history has them.

records.detail: House request system before 2017: in the 2015 session House leaders first required members to fill out detailed request forms (CBS Miami, Apr 1, 2015: "this year House leaders required legislators in that chamber to fill out detailed forms"; the forms totaled more than $2.9 billion); the 2017 House rules then required each project to be filed as its own bill (WFSU, Feb 17, 2017).
